scalars.scalar_value: At least 5 to 7 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in food-service production or another large, complex, multi-unit dining or restaurant environment. Demonstrated success leading and developing substantial frontline workforces and management teams. Experience managing budgets, food and labor costs, procurement, inventory, operational reporting, and financial performance. Strong working knowledge of high-volume food production, quality control, food safety, sanitation, and service delivery. Experience in higher education is valuable but not essential. Pomona welcomes candidates from hospitality, restaurants, corporate dining, healthcare, universities, and other complex food-service environments who can bring fresh thinking to residential college dining.

items.item_text: California ServSafe Food Protection Manager Certification, or the ability to obtain it within 30 days of hire and maintain recertification as required. A valid driver’s license and the ability to meet College vehicle-insurance requirements. Ability to work a flexible schedule that may include evenings, weekends, holidays, and occasional travel, based on program and College needs. Ability to work regularly in active dining and production environments and perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.
Bachelor’s degree in hospitality or restaurant management, business, or a related field.

At least 5 to 7 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in food-service production or another large, complex, multi-unit dining or restaurant environment. Demonstrated success leading and developing substantial frontline workforces and management teams. Experience managing budgets, food and labor costs, procurement, inventory, operational reporting, and financial performance. Strong working knowledge of high-volume food production, quality control, food safety, sanitation, and service delivery. Experience in higher education is valuable but not essential. Pomona welcomes candidates from hospitality, restaurants, corporate dining, healthcare, universities, and other complex food-service environments who can bring fresh thinking to residential college dining.
Provide clear direction and leadership to a large, diverse workforce in a collective bargaining environment.
Recruit, select, onboard, coach, evaluate, and develop leaders and staff across culinary, service, catering, administrative, and support functions.

Build strong relationships with employees; set clear standards for performance, conduct, attendance, communication, and service; recognize excellent work; and address concerns promptly, fairly, and consistently.
Build a collaborative leadership team, strengthen succession planning, and create meaningful opportunities for internal growth.
Coordinate staffing plans and schedules that support service needs, employee well-being, contractual obligations, and responsible labor management.
Plan and lead a comprehensive meal program across board-plan dining, retail operations, cafés, catering, and special events.
Maintain exceptional standards for food quality, variety, presentation, service, cleanliness, sanitation, merchandising, and the condition of facilities and equipment.
Maintain a visible presence in Dining operations, engaging directly with managers, frontline employees, and students to identify opportunities and resolve operational issues.
Oversee menu development and program design in partnership with culinary leaders, addressing diverse tastes, food allergies, special diets, nutrition, wellness, and inclusive dining needs.
Ensure customer concerns are heard and resolved professionally while creating consistent standards of hospitality across the program.
Develop and manage operating budgets based on realistic service, staffing, revenue, and cost assumptions.
Monitor revenues, food and labor costs, purchasing, payroll, invoices, inventory, and other financial and operational reports.
Maintain accurate financial reporting and effective internal controls, and take timely action when performance varies from plan.
Identify responsible cost-management and revenue opportunities without compromising food quality, service, safety, employee well-being, or the student experience.
Oversee inventory controls and the procurement of food, supplies, and equipment within established standards and budgets.
Ensure compliance with applicable food safety, sanitation, occupational safety, health, accessibility, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain strong training, inspection, documentation, and corrective-action practices across all venues.
Ensure equipment and facilities are properly cleaned, maintained, and used, and partner with campus colleagues to address risks and capital needs.
Foster a culture in which employees raise concerns early and leaders respond with urgency, care, and accountability.
Translate the College’s aspirations into a clear, practical, and measurable strategy for Dining Services.
Bring fresh thinking to menus, service models, hours, programming, technology, sustainability, and the use of physical spaces, while testing ideas thoughtfully and measuring results.
Use technology and data to strengthen menu planning, ordering, scheduling, inventory, customer communication, and operating performance.
Advance local and responsible purchasing, sustainability, nutrition, and food-waste reduction within responsible financial parameters.
Collaborate with students, faculty, staff, College offices, vendors, and external partners on programs and cross-campus initiatives.
Represent Dining Services on selected committees and contribute actively to College planning, events, and community life.
Establish meaningful service, financial, workforce, safety, and customer-experience measures, including reliable approaches for understanding student satisfaction.
Maintain appropriate records, prepare reports, analyze trends, and communicate results to College leadership and campus partners.
Pilot promising concepts, evaluate outcomes, and adjust or expand programs based on evidence and community feedback.
Anticipate emerging culinary, consumer, workforce, technology, and sustainability trends and translate them into practical improvements.
